assessment.title: B1 Level Assessment
assessment.description: A comprehensive assessment of B1 grammar, vocabulary, reading, listening, and integrated English use.
assessment.instructions: Complete all sections. Listening passages may be played a maximum of two times. Read carefully and review your answers before submitting.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.option_c: I have visit Berlin last year.
questions.option_d: I did visited Berlin last year.
questions.explanation: Use past simple with 'last year'.

questions.prompt: She's worked here ___ 2022.
questions.explanation: Use since with a starting point.

questions.prompt: At eight, we ___ dinner.
questions.explanation: Use past continuous for an action in progress at a past time.

questions.prompt: I ___ home when I ___ the accident.
questions.explanation: The walk was in progress when the shorter event occurred.

questions.prompt: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll stay home.
questions.explanation: First conditional uses present simple in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: If I ___ more time, I'd learn Japanese.
questions.explanation: Second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause.

questions.prompt: Visitors ___ enter this area. It's prohibited.
questions.explanation: Mustn't expresses prohibition.

questions.prompt: She decided ___ the job offer.
questions.explanation: Decide is followed by an infinitive.

questions.prompt: The woman ___ called earlier is my manager.
questions.explanation: Use who for people.

questions.prompt: The bridge ___ in 1998.
questions.explanation: Past passive uses was/were + past participle.

questions.prompt: Report: 'I can't come.'
questions.option_b: She said me she can't came.
questions.option_d: She said she can't come yesterday always.
questions.explanation: Can commonly backshifts to could.

questions.prompt: The appointment is booked for tomorrow at ten. We ___ the dentist then.
questions.explanation: Present continuous is natural for fixed arrangements.

questions.prompt: What does 'run out of' mean?
questions.explanation: Run out of means have no more.

questions.prompt: Which linker introduces contrast?
questions.explanation: However signals contrast.

questions.prompt: Which word often introduces an unexpected event in a story?
questions.explanation: Suddenly marks an abrupt event.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means an action is optional?
questions.explanation: Don't have to means there is no necessity.

questions.prompt: Which verb pattern is correct?
questions.explanation: Enjoy is followed by a gerund.

questions.prompt: Which pronoun is normally used for a person in a defining relative clause?
questions.explanation: Who refers to people.

questions.prompt: Which structure forms the passive voice?
questions.explanation: The passive uses be + past participle.

questions.prompt: Which expression introduces an example?
questions.explanation: For example introduces an illustration.

questions.prompt: Which sentence contains an error?
questions.option_a: If I had more time, I'd travel.
questions.option_b: If she knew, she'd tell us.
questions.option_c: If he would study more, he'd improve.
questions.option_d: What would you do if you lost your phone?
questions.explanation: Use 'If he studied more'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive sentence.
questions.option_a: The documents are checked every Friday.
questions.option_c: The documents are check every Friday.
questions.option_d: The documents were check every Friday now.
questions.explanation: Present passive uses are + past participle.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct reported statement.
questions.option_b: She said me she was tired.
questions.option_d: She said she is tired yesterday.
questions.explanation: This is the standard reported form.

questions.prompt: Choose the best connector: 'The plan is expensive; ___, it could save time in the long term.'
questions.explanation: However introduces contrast.

passages.title: A Change in Working Life
passages.instructions: Read the text and answer the four questions.
passages.content_text: For most of her career, Elena worked in a traditional office. She started her first full-time job in 2016 and spent nearly seven years commuting every day. In 2023, her company introduced a hybrid system. Since then, Elena has worked from home three days a week and gone to the office on the other two. She says the change has improved her concentration because she can complete detailed tasks more easily at home. However, she still values office days because they give her opportunities to discuss problems informally with colleagues. Last year, she also completed an online project-management course. She has already used several of the techniques from the course, especially when planning deadlines and team responsibilities. Elena does not think remote work is perfect, but in her opinion, the flexibility has made her working life more manageable.

questions.prompt: When did Elena's company introduce hybrid work?
questions.explanation: The text states that the hybrid system began in 2023.

questions.prompt: How long has Elena followed the hybrid system?
questions.explanation: She has used the system since 2023.

questions.prompt: Why does Elena still value office days?
questions.option_b: They allow informal discussion with colleagues
questions.option_d: She has no internet at home
questions.explanation: She values the opportunity for informal problem-solving.

questions.prompt: Which sentence would be incorrect?
questions.option_a: She started her first job in 2016.
questions.option_c: She completed a course last year.
questions.option_d: She has completed the course last year.
questions.explanation: A finished time such as 'last year' requires past simple.

passages.title: A Community Garden Project
passages.instructions: Read the text and answer the four questions.
passages.content_text: A group of residents in Westfield has created a community garden on an empty piece of land beside the library. The project was started by local volunteers after they noticed that many families in the area did not have outdoor space at home. If the first season is successful, the group will add more planting areas next year. Volunteers have to attend a short safety session before using the shared tools, but they do not have to be experienced gardeners. People who are new to gardening can work with volunteers who have more experience. The group also plans to organize weekend workshops. Although the project is still small, the organizers believe it could become an important place for neighbors to meet, learn, and grow food together.

questions.prompt: Who started the project?
questions.explanation: The project was started by local volunteers.

questions.prompt: What will happen if the first season is successful?
questions.option_b: More planting areas will be added
questions.explanation: The group plans to expand next year.

questions.prompt: What do volunteers have to do before using shared tools?
questions.explanation: They must attend a short safety session.

questions.prompt: Who can support new gardeners?
questions.explanation: Experienced volunteers can help them.

passages.title: A Travel Delay
passages.instructions: Listen to the announcement. You may play the audio twice.
passages.audio_text: Attention passengers traveling to Brighton. The 4:20 service is currently delayed because of a technical problem. Engineers were checking the train when they discovered an issue with one of the doors. The train is expected to leave approximately thirty minutes late. If you need to arrive before six, you can take the 4:35 service to Lewes and change there for Brighton. Passengers who decide to use the alternative route will not need to buy another ticket. We apologize for the delay and will provide another update in fifteen minutes.

questions.prompt: Why is the train delayed?
questions.explanation: Engineers discovered a problem with a door.

questions.prompt: What were engineers doing when they found the problem?
questions.explanation: They were checking the train.

questions.prompt: What can passengers do if they need to arrive before six?
questions.option_a: Wait for the delayed train only
questions.option_b: Take an alternative service and change trains
questions.option_d: Take a taxi provided by the station
questions.explanation: An alternative route via Lewes is offered.

questions.prompt: Do passengers using the alternative route have to buy another ticket?
questions.explanation: They do not need another ticket.

passages.title: Discussing a Work Proposal
passages.instructions: Listen to the conversation. You may play the audio twice.
passages.audio_text: I think we should allow the team to work from home two days a week. It could reduce commuting time and help people concentrate. I agree that there are advantages; however, I'm worried about communication. New employees sometimes need quick support. That's true. What if we required everyone to be in the office on Tuesdays and Thursdays? Then teams could plan meetings on those days. That might work. If we try it for three months, we'll have enough information to decide whether to continue. Good idea. I'll prepare a short proposal for the manager.

questions.prompt: What is the first speaker proposing?
questions.explanation: The proposal is two remote days each week.

questions.prompt: What concern does the second speaker raise?
questions.explanation: The concern is communication and support.

questions.prompt: What will they have if they test the system for three months?
questions.explanation: They expect enough information to decide whether to continue.

questions.prompt: What does the final speaker decide to do?
questions.explanation: The speaker decides to prepare a proposal.
